content.title: About
content.content: Dry whole milk is a dehydrated dairy product obtained by evaporating water from whole cow’s milk. When reconstituted with water, it reproduces the properties of regular whole milk, including taste, nutrients, and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dry milk is easy to store and transport because it does not require refrigeration.
Reconstituted dry milk is widely used in the food industry for ice cream, confectionery, and dry mixes.
The fat content in whole dry milk preserves a creamy mouthfeel after reconstitution.
Dry milk has been a staple for military rations and expeditions due to its long shelf life.
When properly reconstituted, dry milk is virtually indistinguishable in flavor from fresh whole milk.

items.title: Rich source of calcium
items.content: Whole dry milk provides a high amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Reconstituted milk contains complete milk protein that supports tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains riboflavin (B2) and vitamin B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Vitamin D content
items.content: Many dry milks are fortified with vitamin D, which aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Convenience and cost‑effectiveness
items.content: Provides whole milk without the need for fresh storage, saving space and money.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dry milk contains lactose, so it should be avoided by people with lactose intolerance or replaced with lactose‑free versions.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey may experience reactions.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Whole dry milk has a relatively high fat level, which may be unsuitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Shelf life after reconstitution
items.content: Reconstituted milk must be kept refrigerated and consumed within a few days.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: To reconstitute, dissolve 1 part dry milk in 4–5 parts cold water, stirring until smooth. The resulting milk can be drunk, used in cooking, added to sauces, cereals, baked goods, and infant formulas.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry milk in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. After reconstitution, keep the milk refrigerated and use within 3–5 days.
